{{Short description|Mexican mathematician}}

{{Family name hatnote|Caballero|Acosta|lang=Spanish}}
'''María Emilia Caballero Acosta''' is a Mexican mathematician specializing in [[probability theory]], including [[Lévy process]]es, [[branching process]]es, [[Markov chain|Markov processes]], and Lamperti representations (an exponential relation between Markov processes and Lévy processes).{{r|im}} She is a professor in the Faculty of Sciences and Researcher in the Institute of Sciences of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).{{r|im|fc}}

==Education and career==
After doing her undergraduate studies at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]],{{r|im}} Caballero went to [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in France for graduate study in mathematics. She completed a [[doctorat de troisième cycle]] in 1973, with the dissertation ''Quelques proprietes en theorie du potentiel'' in [[potential theory]], jointly supervised by Marcel Brelot and [[Paul Malliavin]].{{r|mg}} Her interest in probability theory developed out of this work and the probabilistic theory of potential.{{r|semblanza}}

Already in 1964, she had begun working as an adjunct professor at the [[Escuela Nacional Preparatoria]] and as an assistant in the Faculty of Sciences at UNAM. On completing her doctorate in 1973, she took her present position at the Institute of Mathematics.{{r|semblanza}}

==Recognition==
Caballero is a member of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]].{{r|amc}} She won UNAM's Juana de Asbaje Medal in 2004.{{r|smm}} In 2012 she won UNAM's National University Award, the first woman in the Institute of Mathematics to win this award.{{r|pun}}
